identityEvidence.commonsDescription:
Sarajevo City Hall, Bosnia, April 2026
On 25 August 1992, Serb shelling during the Siege of Sarajevo caused the complete destruction of the city hall; among the losses were about 700 manuscripts and incunabula and a unique collection of Bosnian serial publications, some from the middle of the 19th century Bosnian cultural revival. Before the attack, the city hall held 1.5 million volumes and over 155,000 rare books and manuscripts. Some citizens and librarians tried to save some books while they were under sniper fire, at least one person died. The majority of the books were not saved from the flames.

After it was repaired, the building, now a national monument, has been used for variety of events. Its space has been be used for various protocol events for all levels of government, concerts and exhibitions.

identityEvidence.commonsDescription:
Le triple pont vu de la place Presernov (The three bridges) 
Au fond, la ville ancienne.
Le triple pont (Tromostovje / Three bridges) a été conçu par l'architecte Jože Plečnik en 1929-1932. 
Après la grande guerre, le pont initial était devenu trop étroit pour absorber la circulation entre la ville ancienne et la ville nouvelle.
L'architecte Jože Plečnik proposa de construire de part et d'autre de l'ancien deux nouveaux ponts mais de manière asymétrique pour épouser la courbe faite par la rivière à cet endroit. Des balustrades de type vénitien et des lampadaires d'un style  méditerranéen donnent à l'ensemble des trois ponts un caractère unique qui en a fait depuis lors le centre emblématique de la ville.
